correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact positive product ODE from primary Lemma 3.1 and the unit-round curvature normalization. Let S=A+B,D=A-B. Then Sdot=-S/(3AB), Ddot=-D/(AB), hence d(D/S^3)/dt=0 including D=0. With c=D0/S0^3, A=S(1+cS^2)/2, B=S(1-cS^2)/2 and Sdot=-4/[3S(1-c^2S^4)]. Since |c|S0^2<1 and S decreases, A,B>0 throughout 0<=t<T and S->0 at finite T. Integration gives t=3/8(S0^2-S^2)-c^2/8(S0^6-S^6), monotone in decreasing S and unique. Extinction T=(A0^2+4A0B0+B0^2)/4, also independently follows from d/dt(A^2+4AB+B^2)=-4. Delta=cS^2 yields T-t=S^2(3-delta^2)/8; the delta/c cubic law is restricted to c!=0. Series inversion yields delta=(8c/3)(T-t)+O((T-t)^3); A/B=1+(16c/3)(T-t)+O((T-t)^2). The diagonal case c=0 gives T=3a^2/2. Independent SymPy symbolic checks of all ten identities and inversion coefficients passed; finite checks are supplementary, not the proof.
residual_risks: The audit verifies the primary published product reduction and algebraic ODE conclusion; it does not re-prove the complete fourth-order PDE theory.
The extinction solution stops at T and does not continue as a positive definite metric past T.
